newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal condemns elections in E.Timor.
newsitem.headline: Portugal condemns elections in E.Timor.

text.p: Portugal on Thursday condemned Indonesia's handling of elections in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor, where a wave of political violence killed 14 people overnight.

Portuguese Foreign Minister Jaime Gama, a harsh critic of Indonesia's occupation of the Pacific territory of East Timor, said his government had made a formal complaint to the United Nations and had also made contacts with its European partners.
Millions of Indonesians voted on Thursday in the world's fourth most populous nation.
East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam said a soldier guarding a polling booth was shot dead on Thursday, bringing to 14 the number of deaths in the territory since Wednesday night.

"Elections in Indonesia have not been free elections. In East Timor, an occupied territory, those elections could not have been free, and the people there have shown that they do not accept occupation and annexation," Gama said.
"They want self-determination," he told reporters before the start of a two-day NATO foreign ministers' meeting.
"We have been in contact with the United Nations and we have sent a message to the Secretary General," Gama said. "We are also in contact with our European partners," he added.
The United Nations has never recognised the annexation of East Timor by Indonesia in 1976, a year after it invaded the territory.

The Portuguese government issued a statement, which said: "The government does not recognise any validity in the elections that took place in East Timor on May 29, as a result of the illegal and forced extension to that territory of the legislative elections in Indonesia."
It added: "The occupation of East Timor, repeatedly condemned by U.N. institutions, makes any attempt to gauge the genuine collective will of the Timorese people illegitimate."

The East Timor police chief said police had shot dead four rebels fighting Indonesia's occupation of the territory in a clash in the centre of Dili on Wednesday night during an attempt to disrupt the elections.
He said rebels shot dead at least seven civilians in the town of Los Palos and two in Baucau in separate attacks on Wednesday as opponents of the government destroyed a number of polling booths.
